parts.text: Some students are investigating the link between the brightness of a filament lamp and its resistance. The circuit is shown in Fig. 3.1. Fig. 3.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) On Fig. 3.1, use standard symbols to show a voltmeter connected to measure the potential difference across the lamp. [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The students attach the crocodile clip to various lengths l of the resistance wire and record, in Table 3.1, the potential difference V and the current I for the lamp. They also record observations of the lamp filament. Table 3.1 l / cm V / V I / A observation of lamp filament R / Ω 100 2.5 0.26 bright 60 1.5 0.19 dim 20 0.5 0.11 just glowing Voltmeters with the ranges shown in Fig. 3.2 are available. Fig. 3.2

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) On Fig. 3.2, circle the voltmeter which is most appropriate for this experiment.

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Draw an arrow on this voltmeter to show the reading when the crocodile clip is attached to a length l = 60 cm of the resistance wire. [2]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Calculate, and record in the table, the resistance R of the lamp for each value of l , using the equation R = V I . [2]
